chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abu al-Hasan al-Tamimi from Safwan from Yazid ibn Khalifa said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked while I was with him, and a man said to him: 'My slave threw a basket in my house, and in it are two eggs from the pigeons of the Sanctuary (Haram).' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the value of the two eggs; he should feed them to the pigeons of the Sanctuary.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave damaging or taking eggs from the sacred pigeons of the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *al-Istibsar* illustrates the principle of *diyya* (compensation) for specific sacred assets, highlighting the economic and ritual value of the sanctuary's pigeons in early Islamic Mecca. It underscores the master's responsibility to maintain the sanctity of the Haram by reinvesting the compensation into the pigeons' sustenance, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the integrity of sacred spaces and their associated rights.
